edits.text: 1. PRIVILEGE AND WORK PRODUCT. Defendant objects to production of materials protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, or other applicable protection. Any withholding on these grounds will be identified as required by applicable rules or court order.

2. PRODUCTION. Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents within its possession, custody, or control following a reasonable search, subject to any request-specific objections and in accordance with applicable rules, court orders, and agreements of the parties.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. To the extent required by applicable rules or court order, Defendant will provide a privilege log identifying materials withheld on privilege or work-product grounds and sufficient information to permit assessment of the asserted protection without disclosing protected information.
4. SUPPLEMENTATION. Defendant will supplement these responses as required by applicable rules or court order.

edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant responds to Plaintiff's First Requests for Production. These general provisions do not substitute for request-specific responses. Within seven days after the parties' written agreement on this protocol, and in no event later than the applicable response deadline absent agreement or court order, Defendant will serve supplemental responses addressing each request separately, stating each objection with specificity and whether responsive materials are being withheld on that basis. Each response will identify the portion of the request to which an objection applies and describe any resulting limitation on production. Defendant will state when its search remains ongoing and update its withholding statements upon completion.

1. PRIVILEGE AND WORK PRODUCT. Defendant objects to production of materials protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, or another specifically identified applicable protection. Each request-specific response will state whether responsive materials are being withheld on these grounds. Such materials will be identified in the privilege log described below, except where an exclusion is expressly agreed by the parties or authorized by applicable rules or court order. No objection will excuse production of responsive, non-protected materials outside its scope.

2. SEARCH AND PRODUCTION. Defendant will conduct a reasonable search for responsive documents within its possession, custody, or control. The search will cover custodians reasonably likely to hold responsive materials and their relevant email, business messaging, electronic files, shared repositories, and paper files, within the time periods stated in the requests except as specifically objected to in the supplemental responses. Within seven days after written agreement on this protocol, Defendant will identify the proposed custodians, repositories, date ranges, and search methods, including search terms if used, for prompt conferral. Any proposed exclusion based on burden or accessibility will be identified with its grounds and addressed in the request-specific withholding statements; disputed scope will not delay undisputed searches or production. Defendant will begin production within 14 days after written agreement on this protocol, make additional rolling productions at intervals not exceeding seven days, and complete production within 30 days after that agreement. Production will be in an agreed, reasonably usable format. Defendant proposes searchable PDFs with available extracted text or OCR, native spreadsheets, and native production of other files where needed to preserve usability, with unique production identifiers and preservation of document-family relationships. The parties will confirm format specifications within seven days after agreement on this protocol; unresolved format issues will not delay production in an otherwise agreed format. These provisions do not extend any existing deadline absent agreement or court order. Any extension requires written agreement or court order; notice of a difficulty alone does not extend a deadline.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. Within 14 days after each rolling production, Defendant will provide a log of responsive materials withheld on privilege or work-product grounds during the review associated with that production. Any remaining withheld materials will be logged no later than 14 days after the production-completion deadline. The log will identify each withheld document or redaction by a unique identifier and, where available, its date, document type, author, recipients and their roles, a non-privileged description of the subject matter, the protection asserted, and the basis sufficient to assess the claim without revealing protected information. Any agreed categorical logging or exclusions must be expressly documented in writing; otherwise, exclusions apply only as authorized by applicable rules or court order.

4. SUPPLEMENTATION. Defendant will timely supplement its responses, withholding statements, production, and privilege log as required by applicable rules or court order. At completion of the scheduled production, Defendant will confirm completion of the reasonable search and production described above and identify any unresolved scope issues and any responsive materials still being withheld, with the applicable grounds.
